name: Build dashboard with KPI cards
w: The dashboard must answer two questions in under five seconds: how full am I, and how much money is outstanding. Everything else is decoration.
ac: Cards show total beds, occupied, vacant, occupancy percent, collected this month (IST calendar month) and outstanding
All values are computed live from allocations, invoices and payments
A brand new hostel with no data renders a sensible zero state
Numbers match the occupancy and fee list screens exactly
Loading skeleton prevents layout shift on slow connections
out: No customisable widget layout and no export.

name: Implement occupancy trend read model
w: Owners want to see whether the hostel is filling up or emptying, which a single current snapshot cannot show.
ac: Trend series is derived from allocation start and end dates so history is correct retroactively
Supports day and month granularity
Renders correctly with fewer than 30 days of data
Query cost stays acceptable at 500 beds and 2000 historical allocations
out: No forecasting or seasonal comparison in the MVP.

name: Add recent activity and overdue-fee panels
w: A dashboard that only shows static totals gives nothing to act on. These two panels turn it into a work queue for the day.
ac: Recent allocations, vacates and payments listed with relative timestamps
Overdue residents listed with amount and days overdue
Every item links through to the relevant detail page
Panels handle the empty state without looking broken
out: No configurable alert thresholds in the MVP.

name: Add date-range filter for dashboard metrics
w: Collected and outstanding only make sense for a chosen period, so the range must be explicit and shareable rather than hidden in component state.
ac: Preset ranges for this month, last month and a custom range
Selected range persists in the URL
KPIs recompute correctly across month boundaries
Invalid or reversed ranges are rejected with a clear message
out: No financial year or quarterly rollups.

name: Write RLS test suite covering cross-hostel access attempts
w: Multi-tenant isolation is the one property of this product that must never regress, and manual clicking will not catch it. This task builds the attack harness early, alongside EP-02 and EP-03, and every later table task adds its table to it, so isolation is proven continuously instead of at the end.
ac: A reusable harness creates two hostels with separate owners (and a staff user) through the service role, then attacks with anon-key clients signed in as each user
Covers profiles and hostels on delivery; E4-T1, E5-T1, E6-T1 and E7-T1 each add their tables (select, insert, update and delete)
The suite fails before the policies are applied and passes after
Suite runs locally and in CI on every push
Documented as the required regression gate for any new table
Asserts that an insert pointing at another hostel's parent row (room, bed, resident or invoice) is rejected
ID-proof storage objects are covered once E5-T7 lands
out: No penetration testing or third-party security audit in the MVP.

name: Add integration tests for allocation and fee integrity rules
w: The rules that protect money and beds are the rules most likely to be broken by future refactors, so they get executable guardrails.
ac: Tests cover double allocation rejection, idempotent invoice generation, duplicate room number and duplicate resident
Each test is deterministic against fixtures it creates itself
The whole suite completes in under 60 seconds
Failures name the rule that broke, not just an assertion
Tests run against a local database that is reset between runs
Each rule gets its test when it lands (E4-T4, E5-T3, E6-T3, E7-T3); this task collects and hardens them into one suite
Tests create their own isolated fixtures and never depend on the seed script
out: No UI end-to-end tests for these rules; that is a later Playwright task.

name: Set up CI pipeline for lint, typecheck and tests
w: Solo developers have no reviewer, so the pipeline is the reviewer. It is set up as soon as migrations exist, so every later task is checked from day one instead of discovering broken migrations at the end.
ac: GitHub Actions runs on pull requests and on main
Jobs for lint, typecheck, format check and unit tests, plus the RLS and integration suites against a Supabase stack started in CI by the Supabase CLI as soon as those suites exist
Branch protection on main requires CI to pass, verified with a deliberately failing branch
Status badge visible in the README
Pipeline completes in a reasonable time for a small project
CI fails when the generated database types are out of date with the migrations
out: No automated deployment in this task; deployment is E9-T4.

name: Deploy staging to Vercel with a separate Supabase environment
w: A shareable staging URL is how the product gets in front of the first real hostel owner, and separate environments prevent test data from polluting real money records.
ac: Staging URL is live and accessible
Environment variables configured in Vercel and never committed
All migrations applied to the staging database
Supabase staging project is separate from any future production project
Smoke test grows with each epic; the final version covers signup, create hostel, add a room, add a resident, allocate a bed, generate an invoice and record a payment
First deployed as soon as login works (after E2-T3) and redeployed continuously, so deployment problems surface early rather than at the end
Custom SMTP configured on the staging Supabase project, because the built-in email service only delivers to project team members
Supabase Auth Site URL and redirect URLs set to the staging and preview domains, so confirmation and reset links work
Vercel Node version matches .nvmrc (24)
Migrations are applied to staging with supabase db push, documented as a runbook in the README
README notes that free-tier Supabase projects pause after a week of inactivity
out: No production domain or custom DNS in this task. The Vercel CLI is not installed on this machine yet.

name: Add error logging and a global error boundary
w: A solo developer cannot debug what they cannot see, but logs must never capture resident personal data or credentials.
ac: Unhandled errors render a friendly page instead of a stack trace
Server-side errors are logged with request context and a correlation id
Logs contain no personal data, tokens or service keys, verified by inspecting a sample failure
A deliberate test route proves the boundary catches and logs the error
Builds on the existing (app)/error.tsx and the navigation pending indicator; no route-level loading.tsx (see AppShell)
out: No paid monitoring or alerting service in the MVP.

name: Add idempotent local seed script
w: Every realistic test and every UI decision needs data. A one command seed removes the temptation to click through setup twenty times a day.
ac: One command seeds a hostel, 40 beds, 25 residents, live allocations and invoices
Re-running does not duplicate data
Seed output prints the login credentials for the seeded owner
Started alongside EP-04 and extended by each schema epic; the test suites do not depend on it
